dependencies.reason: uses its router and the external URL its configuration source provides
authenticates git clients with its credentials and checks a PAT's git scopes
applies its access decision, reads the settings that govern push control, and honours its bound-token confinement

tasks.title: Serve the git routes and authenticate their clients
steps: Establish whether isomorphic-git exposes pkt-line framing for the advertisement, the receive-pack command list and the per-ref report, or whether it must be written from the protocol documentation, and record the finding
Add this task's behaviours to the git server and git auth test files, and confirm they fail
Serve the three git routes under /git/<org>/<slug>.git at the server root, outside the mount point
Answer a path without the .git suffix, a mismatched organization and an unknown slug with one identical pkt-line 404 ERR repository not found
Accept the HTTP Basic password as a hub credential and ignore the username, refusing a missing, invalid, revoked or blocked credential with a pkt-line 401
Express every git refusal in pkt-line framing rather than the JSON error envelope
Mint a repo-scoped store token per relay, never accept one from a client and never let one reach a response body, header or log record
Make a workspace's hub_url report exactly the address served, and null where there is no organization or no external URL

tasks.title: Apply the hub's access rules to git requests
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the git access test files, and confirm they fail
Run the checks in order: the workspace and its organization against the URL, then that the repository is ready, then access, then a PAT's git scope
Serve a fetch to the owner, an admin token and a member alike, and a push to the owner and an admin token
Refuse a member's push and receive-service advertisement with the pkt-line 403 member message, before the PAT's scopes are considered
Answer a stranger and a token bound to another workspace with the pkt-line 404, identically for a workspace that exists, one that is archived and one that does not
Answer a failed access lookup with a pkt-line 500 and serve nothing
Check git:read for a fetch and git:write for a push, with git:write granting git:read

tasks.title: Serve clones and fetches by relaying to the store
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the git server test files, and confirm they fail
Serve the ref advertisement for both services with the documented content types, relaying to the store
Refuse a missing, empty or unknown service parameter with the pkt-line 403 and the documented message
Relay the upload-pack negotiation so that a fetch transfers only the objects the client lacks
Serve whichever protocol version the client asks for among those the store speaks, and accept a gzip-encoded request body
Confirm against a real git client that the advertisement and the pack are accepted

tasks.title: Accept pushes and report every ref
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the git push test files, and confirm they fail
Read the push's ref command list from the request before relaying any of it
Relay the accepted commands to the store with the minted token and apply them
Merge the store's per-ref report with any refusals this service made, so the client receives one report covering every ref it sent
Confirm by test that the set of refs whose value changed equals the set reported ok
Leave the repository untouched when a push is refused outright

tasks.title: Decide each patch branch before it reaches the store
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the push control integration test file, and confirm they fail
Identify a registered patch branch from the workspace's patch list, excluding deleted patches and the integration branch
With patch_branch_source origin and push_patches_to_origin false, refuse an update with the documented message naming git_url without its userinfo, and a deletion with the delete-on-the-fork message

With patch_branch_source origin and push_patches_to_origin true, push the update to the fork first without forcing and accept it only on the fork's acceptance, reporting origin rejected push or a credential failure otherwise, and refusing a deletion
With patch_branch_source hub and push_patches_to_origin true, accept the update and then force-push it to the fork, letting a failed mirror leave the push successful
With patch_branch_source hub and push_patches_to_origin false, on a standard workspace, or for a ref that is not a registered patch branch, apply no push control
Decide each ref of a push on its own, so one ref's refusal does not affect another's outcome

tasks.title: Protect the hub's own ref namespace
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the protected namespace test files, and confirm they fail
Refuse every client create, update and delete of a ref under refs/hub/replaced/, reporting unpack ok and the fixed ng message for that ref while the rest of the push proceeds
Apply the protection on every workspace and for every credential, an admin token included
Serve those refs to a fetch where the store's capability report says the namespace is accepted, and report the read as unavailable where it is not, without weakening the push refusal

tasks.title: Refresh the workspace after a push
steps: Add this task's behaviours to the git push test files, and confirm they fail
Refresh the workspace's head_sha from the repository's HEAD after every push, including one whose every ref was refused
Confirm that a refused ref triggers no forward, no mirror and no other change to the workspace record
Leave a documented place for package 09 to queue a rebuild for an accepted patch branch, without adding one here

tasks.title: Drive a real git client against a running deployment
steps: Add the four smoke tests and confirm each passes against a running deployment with a real git binary, or skips with a message naming what was missing

Trace 07-PATH-1: the clone authenticates through package 02, is admitted by package 03's access decision, mints a store token and relays to package 05's store; the push returns through push control and refreshes head_sha
Trace 07-PATH-2: the member's fetch and the member's refused push both reach the same access decision, and no object reaches the store for the refused push
Trace 07-PATH-3: push control reads the real patch list and the real settings, and the merged per-ref report reaches the git client
Trace 07-PATH-4: the protected namespace refusal is produced before anything is relayed, and the ordinary ref of the same push is applied

For every criterion carrying a contract, confirm a caller in production code consumes the producer's result and not only a test: the pkt-line writer is used by every refusal, the access decision by every route, the credential resolution by the forward and the mirror, and the capability report by the protected-namespace read
Confirm afc credential-helper plus a plain git clone of hub_url works, which is the Quick Tour of docs/prd/cli.md
Grep src/git/ and the files every task's touches lists for TODO, FIXME and the project's not-implemented marker, and remove any that remain
Add the git server conformance cases to the harness from package 01
done_when: `make check` passes with no network access and no deployment configured
git clone, git fetch and git push against hub_url succeed with the afc credential helper on a running deployment
